hero.title: Systematic reviews: the AI extracts the data, you verify it.
hero.lede: Krinea keeps your whole systematic review in one place, from importing references to the PRISMA 2020 diagram. For extraction, the AI fills in your form and quotes the exact sentence behind each value, so you only have to check. Open source, alone or as a team.
hero.note: No credit card. AGPL-3.0. Hosted in Frankfurt (EU) or on your own server.

how.title: One review, five stages.
how.lede: A systematic review goes through five stages, and Krinea keeps them in one workspace from which everything can be exported at any time. The screens below are the real application, on a sample review of 55 fictitious records.

import.title: Import every search export.
import.b1: Drop in your RIS, BibTeX, PubMed, Web of Science, CSV, TSV or Excel files: the format is recognised on upload.
import.b2: Each file is kept as a separate batch, with its source database and the date it came in.
import.b3: From that first import, the counts per source start feeding the PRISMA diagram.
import.alt: Data page of a review: three count tiles, the import box and a table of two imported files

dedup.title: Remove duplicates, keep the evidence.
dedup.b1: References that share a DOI or a title are merged on their own.
dedup.b2: When the resemblance is less clear, Krinea shows you both records side by side with their similarity score, and you make the call.
dedup.alt: Duplicates panel with two similarity sliders and pairs of near-identical records to check

screen.title: Screen the studies, alone or as a team.
screen.b1: Screening starts on title and abstract and moves on to full text, with your keywords highlighted and the I, M and E shortcuts to keep the pace.
screen.b2: In double screening, each reviewer decides without seeing the others' choice; the disagreements are then gathered in one list to be settled.
screen.b3: Every decision is recorded with its reason, its author and its time.
screen.alt: Screening view: the record list with progress, a record card with highlighted keywords and the Include, Maybe and Exclude buttons

extract.title: Extract with quotes you can check.
extract.b1: You design the form, then the AI fills it in from each PDF.
extract.b2: Every proposed value comes with the exact passage it was taken from, so you can check it without reopening the paper.
extract.b3: Until a person has validated it, a value is only a proposal.
extract.alt: Extraction form with values and, under each value, the sentence it was taken from

report.title: Report with the official PRISMA 2020 diagram.
report.b1: The diagram's counts are computed from your decisions, so there is nothing to retype.
report.b2: You can then download the diagram as SVG, the included studies as RIS or CSV and the validated extractions as Excel.
report.b3: The decision log exports too, for traceability.
report.alt: PRISMA 2020 page: six count tiles, the Download SVG button and the top of the flow diagram

story.title: Built by a researcher who needed it.
story.p1: Krinea began as a script written during a real systematic review on long-term energy-system models in Africa. Its author needed to pull structured data out of hundreds of PDFs without losing track of where each value came from. The script grew a form, then a quote next to every value, then a screening step so the same team could decide which papers to read at all.
story.p2: Today Krinea is an independent open-source project maintained by one developer-researcher based in France, with no company behind it. The hosted edition runs in Frankfurt and is free while it is in beta. The code is AGPL-3.0, so whatever happens to the hosted edition, you can run it yourself.

two.title: Built for teams, disagreements included.
two.lede: Most reviews are done by several people, and that is exactly what Krinea was designed for. Each reviewer works on their own, blind if the review calls for it, and the disagreements are then gathered in one list where they can be settled with full context, while everyone's progress stays visible.
two.f1: Single or double screening, chosen per review, whatever the size of the team.
two.f2: Blind mode applies at every stage, on title and abstract as on full text.
two.f3: A disagreement is settled with both decisions and their reasons on screen, and the final call is logged.
two.link: Invite a colleague from the review settings
two.alt: Two colleagues going through a printed report together at a desk

principles.title: Six things Krinea will not change its mind about.

ai.title: The AI suggests. A person decides.
ai.text: Its suggestions are stored apart from the decisions, so they never count as one until someone has made them their own.

reason.title: Every decision keeps its reason.
reason.text: Whether it is an inclusion, an exclusion or a doubt, the reason, the author and the time go into a log you can export.

blind.title: Double screening is blind.
blind.text: Each reviewer decides without seeing the other's choice, and only once both decisions are in do the disagreements show up.

yours.title: Your data leaves when you want.
yours.text: References, the decision log, extractions and the PRISMA diagram export as RIS, CSV or Excel, at any time and without a subscription.

open.title: Open source, for good.
open.text: The application is released under AGPL-3.0 and the engine under MIT, so you can host it yourself with Docker Compose or the Render blueprint.

lang.title: In French and in English.
lang.text: The interface, the e-mails and this site were written in both languages, separately rather than machine-translated.

faq.title: Questions people ask first.
faq.more: Anything else: <contact>write to us</contact> or <discussions>open a discussion on GitHub</discussions>.

free.a: Yes. While Krinea is in beta, the hosted edition is free with every feature, and self-hosting will stay free whatever happens. The Pro and Institution plans will only open once billing and the legal documents are ready, and nothing is charged unless you subscribe yourself.

data.a: Your data is hosted in Frankfurt, Germany, on servers run by Render. If you install Krinea on your own infrastructure, it stays wherever you put it. The privacy policy details what is kept and for how long.

import.q: Can I import from Zotero, EndNote or Mendeley?
import.a: Yes, through an export. Your reference manager can produce a RIS or BibTeX file, which Krinea reads directly, as it does PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus exports. A direct Zotero connection does not exist yet.

conflict.q: What happens when two reviewers disagree?
conflict.a: The record is then flagged as a disagreement. Both decisions appear side by side with their reasons, and the person responsible for the review makes the final call. Every vote stays in the decision log.

ai.a: No. It proposes a decision with a reason, or fills in an extraction form quoting a passage for each field, but its proposals are stored apart and only a person can include, exclude or validate. You use your own API key for this.

selfhost.a: Yes. The repository ships a Docker Compose file and a Render blueprint, and since the application is under AGPL-3.0 and the engine under MIT, nothing stops you from installing it on your own servers.

closing.title: Start your first review. It is free.
closing.lede: Import a first search export, invite a colleague if you like, and move forward knowing that everything stays exportable, from day one.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lede: Every message is read by a real person, in French or in English. Bugs and feature requests move fastest on GitHub, while institutional requests, free access and anything private go by e-mail.

institutions.title: Institutions
institutions.text: Single sign-on, admin console, invoicing and a data processing agreement for universities and organisations. Tell us the number of reviewers, the review types and your data requirements.

lowIncome.title: Free Pro access
lowIncome.text: Reviewers at institutions in low-income countries get the Pro plan for free. Write from your institutional e-mail address with your name and department.

support.title: Support and bugs
support.text: The issue tracker is public: search it first, then open an issue with what you did, what you expected and what happened. Questions and ideas go to Discussions. Security vulnerabilities never go in a public issue: report them privately by e-mail or through GitHub private vulnerability reporting.

contact.response: We answer within five working days; there is no phone line or live chat.

seo.title: Krinea: open-source systematic review software
seo.description: Import references, remove duplicates, screen titles and abstracts with your team, extract data with an AI that quotes its sources, and report with the official PRISMA 2020 diagram. Free to self-host, hosted in the EU.
